If a job uses port 22, a hint with the button Use port 23 appears. It switches the port, asks you to trust the host key of port 23 and checks the destination. If port 23 does not work, Keepsake switches back to port 22. Both ports reach the same storage, so an existing repository is found on either port.

docs.title: Repository password
docs.text:
Field When to fill it Repository password (encrypts the backups) Always for a new job. For an existing job only if you change the destination or want to enter the password again. Repeat password (only needed for a new repository) Only when Keepsake creates a new repository.
  • New repository: the password needs at least 8 characters, and both fields must match.
  • Existing repository: enter the password that repository already has. The Repeat password field is not needed. If the password is wrong, the job is not saved.

The repository password is stored on this server, protected by Windows, so scheduled backups can run. Keepsake never shows stored passwords again. What the password and the recovery key are for is explained in Passwords and keys.

docs.title: Check destination
docs.text:
Check destination tests the destination with the values on the tab, without saving. The result appears in the box below the buttons:

Line Meaning Location The resolved location, for example the USB path with its current drive letter. Repository found, password correct – N snapshot(s). An existing repository opens with the entered or stored password. Repository found. A repository exists, but no password was tested. No repository yet – a new encrypted repository is created when you save. The location is empty. Writable, deletable · N GB free Keepsake can write and delete there. Free space is shown where the destination reports it. Writable, but files cannot be deleted Backups work, but cleanup of old backups will not. NOT writable Backups will fail. Encryption: ... – strong / good / weak SFTP only: the negotiated encryption. See below. Further lines Problems, for example a wrong password or a share that cannot be reached.

The encryption rating describes the SSH connection, not the backups, which are always encrypted by Keepsake:

  • strong: authenticated encryption (AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305) with a modern key exchange.
  • good: AES-CTR with HMAC-SHA2. A note explains that the server offers no authenticated encryption.
  • weak: CBC, 3DES or SHA-1. Ask the server administrator to enable stronger algorithms.

For USB destinations, the check uses the first connected disk.

docs.title: Copy for KeePass
docs.text: Copy for KeePass copies a text block for the job's KeePass entry: job name, location, SFTP host key, which logins belong in the entry, the repository ID (after a check), this computer's name and how to restore. It contains no passwords and no recovery key. Paste it into KeePass and add the repository password, the recovery key and the storage login there.

docs.title: Create the repository and store the recovery key
docs.text:
When you save a job whose destination holds no repository, Keepsake asks Create a new encrypted repository on ... ?. After you confirm, the window Store your recovery key shows the recovery key once.

Button What it does Copy KeePass entry Copies the same text block as Copy for KeePass, plus the recovery key on a line of its own. Copy key only Copies only the key. Save as file… Saves the KeePass text block, including the key, as a text file readable only by you. Move it off this server, for example as an attachment of the KeePass entry.

Keepsake clears the clipboard two minutes after copying. Done becomes available once you tick I have stored the recovery key in a safe place outside this server. If you close the window without ticking it, Keepsake asks for confirmation.

Warning

The repository password and the recovery key are the only ways to open the backups. Without them, the backups cannot be restored. Test them later with Check keys on the job card.

If you cancel the confirmation, the job is not saved.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: The Options tab holds the settings that change how a job runs: catch-up after downtime, VSS shadow copies, retries, commands before and after the backup, and credentials for network shares the job reads from. Two related settings are elsewhere: Enabled (scheduled runs active) at the top of the job editor, and the e-mail notifications on the Retention & checks tab.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Option Default Allowed Run a missed backup once after the server starts (e.g. after it was switched off) on Use VSS snapshots so open and locked files are backed up (recommended) on Retry … times, after … minutes 2 times, 15 minutes 0 to 10 times, 1 minute to 24 hours Command before the backup empty Command after the backup empty Command timeout 30 minutes 1 minute to 24 hours Network shares used as sources none

docs.title: Enable or disable the job
docs.text: Enabled (scheduled runs active) sits next to the job name at the top of the editor. Clear it to stop all scheduled runs, catch-up runs, retries and "no successful backup" alerts of the job, for example while a server is being migrated. See The Backup jobs page for what a disabled job can still do.

docs.title: Missed backups
docs.text: With Run a missed backup once after the server starts (e.g. after it was switched off) on, a scheduled run that was missed while the server or the service was down starts once after the service starts again. Turn it off if a backup during working hours would disturb users. Details: Schedule.

docs.title: VSS shadow copies
docs.text:
With Use VSS snapshots so open and locked files are backed up (recommended) on, Keepsake creates a Volume Shadow Copy of each local drive that holds a source and reads the files from it. Open and locked files, such as Outlook data files or databases, are backed up in the state they had when the shadow copy was taken. The shadow copies are deleted after the run.

  • VSS is used for local fixed drives only. Sources on network shares are read directly. For a removable drive, Keepsake reads the files directly and adds a warning.
  • If a shadow copy cannot be created, the backup does not fail. Keepsake reads the files directly and adds the warning VSS snapshot could not be created (...). Files are read directly; open or locked files may be skipped. The run then ends with warnings.
  • With VSS off, locked files are skipped and listed in the run log.

Leave VSS on unless a specific application has problems with shadow copies.

docs.title: Retries
docs.text: When a scheduled backup fails, Keepsake waits the given number of minutes and tries again, up to the given number of times. 0 turns retries off. Retries apply to scheduled and caught-up backups only; a backup you start manually is not retried. See Schedule.

docs.title: Commands before and after the backup
docs.text:
Use the commands to prepare the data, for example to dump a database into a folder the job backs up, or to stop and restart a service.

Field When it runs Command before the backup (cmd.exe; a non-zero exit code cancels the backup) Before the VSS shadow copy is taken and before the repository is opened. Command after the backup (always runs; KEEPSAKE_STATUS holds success / warning / failed) After the backup, whatever the result: also after a failed or cancelled backup and after a failed pre-command.

How the commands run:

  • Through cmd.exe /c, as the service account LocalSystem (SYSTEM), with C:\Windows\System32 as working directory. Use full paths for scripts and programs.
  • Mapped drive letters are not available. Use UNC paths, and remember that SYSTEM reaches network shares with the computer account.
  • If a command runs longer than Command timeout, Keepsake ends it together with all processes it started. A pre-command that times out fails the run.
  • A pre-command that ends with an exit code other than 0 fails the run: The pre-command failed with exit code N. The backup was not started. A failed scheduled run is retried as usual.
  • A post-command that ends with an exit code other than 0 turns a successful run into a run with warnings. It does not change a failed run.
  • The output of both commands and their exit codes appear in the run log in History and logs.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Keepsake passes these variables to both commands:

Variable Content KEEPSAKE_JOB The job name. KEEPSAKE_RUN_ID The ID of the run, as shown in the history. KEEPSAKE_MODE incremental or full. KEEPSAKE_REPOSITORY The destination as text, for example E:\Backups\Fileserver, USB disk Backup1 \Keepsake or sftp://backup@host/backups/fileserver.

The post-command also gets:

Variable Content KEEPSAKE_STATUS success, warning or failed; cancelled if the backup was cancelled. KEEPSAKE_SNAPSHOT The ID of the new snapshot, or empty if no snapshot was created.

Job names and paths can contain spaces, so always quote the variables:

C:\Scripts\after-backup.cmd "%KEEPSAKE_JOB%" "%KEEPSAKE_STATUS%"

"C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin\pg_dump.exe" -U backup -f "D:\Dumps\app.sql" app

Warning

The commands run with full SYSTEM rights. Only enter commands and scripts that only administrators can change.

docs.title: Network shares used as sources
docs.text:
For each network share the job reads from, you can store an account of its own. Click Add share and fill in:

Column Content Share (\server\share) The share itself, \\server\share, without subfolders. User (DOMAIN\user) DOMAIN\user or server\user. Password The password. For a stored password the field stays empty; leave it empty to keep it.

Without an entry, the service connects with the computer account (DOMAIN\SERVER$). The credentials are used only for the connection to that share. Credentials for a destination share are entered on the Destination tab instead. Remove deletes an entry.

docs.title: Retention and checks
docs.text: The Retention & checks tab decides which backups a job keeps, how often old backups are removed to free space, how often the repository is verified, and when Keepsake sends e-mail about the job.

docs.title: Which backups to keep
docs.text:
Each rule keeps some snapshots. A snapshot is kept if any rule keeps it. 0 turns a rule off. If all rules are 0, Keepsake keeps every snapshot and never removes anything.

Rule Keeps Last backups The N newest snapshots. One per day, for … days The newest snapshot of each of the last N days that have a snapshot. One per week, for … weeks The newest snapshot of each of the last N weeks (Monday to Sunday) that have a snapshot. One per month, for … months The newest snapshot of each of the last N calendar months that have a snapshot. One per year, for … years The newest snapshot of each of the last N calendar years that have a snapshot. Everything from the last … days Every snapshot younger than N days, counted from the time of the cleanup.

Days, weeks, months and years are counted in local time and only where a snapshot exists. A day without a backup (for example a weekend) does not use up one of the N days. Allowed values are 0 to 10000.

A new job starts with 14 days, 8 weeks and 12 months; the other rules are 0.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A job backs up every evening at 22:00 and keeps One per day, for 14 days, One per week, for 8 weeks and One per month, for 12 months.

  • The daily rule keeps the snapshots of the 14 most recent days.
  • The weekly rule keeps the newest snapshot of each of the 8 most recent weeks. For the last two weeks these are snapshots the daily rule keeps anyway; for the six weeks before, it keeps the Sunday snapshot.
  • The monthly rule keeps the newest snapshot of each of the 12 most recent months, that is the snapshot of the last day of each month.

Together the job keeps about 30 snapshots: every day for two weeks, then one per week for about two months, then one per month for a year. All other snapshots are removed at the next cleanup.

docs.title: Protected backups
docs.text: Protected snapshots are never removed by the retention rules. You protect a snapshot on the Restoring files page with Protect this backup (and remove it with Remove protection).

docs.title: Rules apply to this job's snapshots only
docs.text:
Every snapshot records the name the job had when it was created. Retention, the cleanup preview and Clean up only consider snapshots with the job's current name.

Renaming a job

If you rename a job, snapshots created under the old name are no longer covered by retention. They stay in the repository until you remove them. Avoid renaming jobs that already have backups, and never give two jobs that share a repository the same name.

docs.title: Preview the cleanup
docs.text: Click Preview cleanup to see what the next cleanup would remove with the values currently on the tab, before you save. The list shows each snapshot with keep or REMOVE, its time and the rules that keep it (for example daily 2026-11-20, weekly 2026-11-16, protected). The preview works for saved jobs that have backups; for a new job the button is not available.

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
Clean up every … days (after a backup; 0 = never) controls the automatic cleanup. Default: 7 days.

After every backup that ends with OK or with warnings, Keepsake checks whether the last cleanup is older than this interval. If so, it queues a cleanup right after the backup. A cleanup only runs if the job has at least one retention rule.

A cleanup:

  1. removes the snapshots that no rule keeps,
  2. deletes stored data that no remaining snapshot needs, including data left over by interrupted backups,
  3. repacks files in the repository that are at least 25 % unused, so the space is actually freed.

The run's message shows how many snapshots were removed and how much space was freed. If the repository has missing data, the cleanup stops without changing anything and asks you to run a check first.

To clean up immediately, click Clean up on the job card on the Backup jobs page.

Note

Cleanup needs permission to delete files at the destination. Check destination on the Destination tab tells you if deleting is not possible.

docs.title: Integrity checks
docs.text:
Check every … days, reading … % of the data controls the automatic check. Defaults: every 7 days, 10 %.

  • Every check verifies the structure of the repository: index, snapshots and that all referenced data exists.
  • In addition, the given share of stored data is read, decrypted and compared with its checksum. Each check picks a random sample, so over time all data gets verified. 0 % checks the structure only; 100 % reads everything.

After every backup that ends with OK or with warnings, Keepsake checks whether the last check is older than the interval and, if so, queues a check after the backup (and after a cleanup, if one is due). 0 days turns automatic checks off. Since a new job has no check yet, the first check runs after its first backup.

To check immediately, click Check on the job card. A manual check reads the same percentage.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
E-mail notifications are configured per job on this tab. They need a working mail server on the Settings page.

Option Sends a mail when When a run fails A backup, check or cleanup fails. Default: on. When a run has warnings (files not backed up) A run ends with warnings. Default: on. After every successful backup A backup ends without problems. Default: off. Alert if no successful backup for … hours (0 = off) No backup ended with OK or with warnings for this many hours. Default for a new job: 48.

The "no successful backup" alert also catches a stopped schedule or a job that keeps failing. It is repeated once per alert period while the situation lasts, and it is not sent while the job is running. A disabled job sends no alert. See Monitoring and notifications for the mail content.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text: The Schedule tab decides when a job runs automatically. A job can have several schedule entries, each with its own times and its own backup type. A job without entries runs only when you start it.

docs.title: Add and edit entries
docs.text:
The list on the left shows all entries as text, for example daily at 22:00 (incremental) or Sat at 23:00 (full). Select an entry to edit it on the right.

  • Add schedule adds an entry: daily at 22:00, incremental.
  • Remove deletes the selected entry.
  • Schedule active switches a single entry off without deleting it. The list then shows – disabled after it.

A new job starts with one entry, daily at 22:00, incremental. The schedule only works while the job itself is enabled (Enabled (scheduled runs active) at the top of the editor).

docs.title: Schedule kinds
docs.text:
Choose the kind under Repeat.

Kind Fields Runs Daily At (HH:mm, several separated by commas), On (none ticked = every day) At each time, on the ticked weekdays. No weekday ticked means every day. Interval Every … minutes (at least 5) Repeatedly, every N minutes. Allowed: 5 minutes to 7 days (10080 minutes). Monthly At (HH:mm, ...), On days of the month (e.g. 1, 15; 31 = last day) At each time, on each listed day of the month.

Times are local times in 24-hour format, for example 22:00 or 6:30, 12:30, 18:30.

Monthly and short months: a day that does not exist in a month runs on the last day of that month. 31 runs on 30 April and on 28 or 29 February; 30 also runs on the last day of February.

Interval timing: the interval counts from the last scheduled start of this entry, not from the end of the run and not from manual runs. A new interval entry first runs one interval after you save it.

Note

A new entry never starts a run immediately when you save. The service starts counting from the moment it first sees the entry. If you change the time of an existing entry to a time that already passed today, and the entry has not run since that time, the service treats it as a missed run.

docs.title: Backup type per entry
docs.text:
Each entry has a Backup type: Incremental or Full.

  • Incremental reads only files whose size or modification time changed.
  • Full re-reads every file. It is slower but catches files that changed without a new modification time.

Every backup is a complete snapshot either way, and only new data is stored.

If several entries are due at the same time, Keepsake starts one run. It is a full backup if at least one of the due entries is Full.

docs.title: Typical setup
docs.text:
Entry Repeat Settings Backup type 1 Daily At 22:00, Mon to Fri ticked Incremental 2 Daily At 22:00, Sat ticked Full

This gives a fast incremental backup on working days and a full backup once a week. If you prefer a daily backup also on Saturday, leave all weekdays unticked in entry 1: on Saturday both entries are due and Keepsake runs one full backup.

docs.title: Missed runs after downtime
docs.text:
A scheduled run is "missed" when its time passed more than 5 minutes ago without a run, for example because the server was switched off or the service was stopped.

With Run a missed backup once after the server starts (e.g. after it was switched off) on the Options tab (default: on), the service starts the backup once shortly after it starts again. Several missed times are caught up with a single run, not one run per missed time. With the option off, the missed run is skipped and Keepsake writes a warning (event ID 1003) to the Windows Application event log.

docs.title: Retries after a failure
docs.text:
When a scheduled backup fails, Keepsake retries it. Set this on the Options tab under When a scheduled backup fails: Retry N times, after M minutes (default: 2 times after 15 minutes; 0 to 10 retries, 1 minute to 24 hours delay).

  • Retries apply to scheduled and caught-up runs, not to backups you start with Run now or Full backup.
  • A retry uses the same backup type as the failed run.
  • Cancelled runs and runs with warnings are not retried.
  • The card's Next line shows the time of a pending retry.

docs.title: A run is due while the job is still running
docs.text: A job never runs twice at the same time. If an entry becomes due while the same job is still running or queued, that scheduled run is skipped. Keepsake logs it in the service log and writes a warning (event ID 1003) to the Windows Application event log. The next occurrence runs as usual.

docs.title: Manual-only jobs
docs.text:
Remove all entries to make a job manual-only (the tab says No schedule = manual runs only.). The job card then shows Manual only and No schedule. Start the backups with Run now or Full backup on the Backup jobs page, or from the command line.

Tip

A manual-only job can still alert you when nobody has run it for a while: set Alert if no successful backup for … hours on the Retention & checks tab.

docs.title: What to back up and exclusions
docs.text: The tabs What to back up and Exclusions of the job editor decide which files a job saves. You tick folders and files in a tree, untick what you do not need inside them, and add patterns for files that should never be backed up, such as temporary files.

docs.title: Select folders and files
docs.text:
The tree on the What to back up tab lists the drives of this computer. Expand a drive or folder to see its content.

  • Tick a folder or file to back it up. A ticked folder includes everything below it, including folders created later.
  • Untick an item inside a ticked folder to exclude it. This is an "exclusion by selection".
  • Folder hints help you find your selection in a collapsed tree: some items excluded on a ticked folder, contains selected items on an unticked folder.

The right side lists the result:

  • Backed up: the top-level sources of the job. Remove takes a source out.
  • Excluded by selection: items unticked inside a source. Include again removes the exclusion.

You cannot tick an item inside a folder you unticked. Keepsake then shows This item is inside an excluded folder. Tick that folder again to include it.

docs.title: Add network paths and paths not in the tree
docs.text:
Enter the path in the field Add a path that is not in the tree (e.g. \server\share\folder) and click Add. The path must be absolute: D:\Data or \\server\share\folder.

Use UNC paths, not mapped drive letters

The tree shows the drives of your own session, including mapped network drives. The Keepsake service runs as LocalSystem and does not see your mapped drives. Add network sources as \\server\share\folder.

docs.title: Credentials for network shares
docs.text: The service reaches a share with the computer account (DOMAIN\SERVER$) unless you store credentials. To use another account, open the Options tab and add the share under Network shares used as sources with Share (\server\share), User (DOMAIN\user) and Password. The credentials are used only for the connection to that share.

docs.title: Exclusion patterns
docs.text:
On the Exclusions tab, enter patterns in Exclusion patterns – one per line. Matching files and folders are skipped; a matching folder is skipped with everything inside it. Upper and lower case do not matter.

Pattern Matches *.tmp Every file or folder whose name ends in .tmp, anywhere. ~$* Office lock files such as ~$Report.docx. Thumbs.db Every file or folder with exactly this name. cache\ Every folder named cache, anywhere. Files named cache are kept. D:\Data\Temp Exactly this path. D:\Data\**\obj\ Every folder named obj at any depth below D:\Data. bin\Debug Debug directly inside a bin folder, at any depth.

The rules:

  • Without \ the pattern matches the file or folder name. Here * matches any characters and ? one character.
  • A trailing \ restricts the pattern to folders.
  • With \ the pattern matches the full path. * and ? stay within one folder level; ** spans any number of levels. A path pattern that does not start with a drive letter, \\ or ** matches at any depth.
  • / is treated like \.
  • Lines starting with # are ignored.

Regular expressions, size limits and age limits are not supported.

Note

Comment lines (#) are not kept when you save the job. A plain full path that lies inside a source, such as D:\Data\Temp, appears under Excluded by selection the next time you open the job.

There is no preview of which files a pattern matches. To see what was excluded, run the backup and look at the run in History and logs.

docs.title: Standard system items
docs.text:
Also exclude the standard system items is on by default. It excludes:

  • $RECYCLE.BIN\
  • System Volume Information\
  • pagefile.sys, hiberfil.sys, swapfile.sys
  • ~$*

Leave it on unless you have a reason to back up these items.

docs.title: Special files and folders
docs.text:
• Junctions and symbolic links to folders are not followed. Keepsake records a warning Junction or symbolic link – the linked folder is not followed. and the link itself is not backed up. Back up the target folder directly if you need it. The tree hides such folders.
  • Long paths: paths longer than 260 characters are read and backed up.
  • Open and locked files are read from a VSS shadow copy when Use VSS snapshots so open and locked files are backed up (recommended) is on (see Options). Without VSS, a locked file is skipped with the message File is locked by another program. Enable VSS for the job to back up open files. and the run ends with warnings.
  • Unreadable files (for example Access denied.) are skipped and listed as not backed up in the run log; the run ends with warnings. The rest of the backup continues.

docs.title: The Backup jobs page
docs.text: The Backup jobs page is the start page of Keepsake. It shows one card per job with its current state, the last run, the schedule and the next run, and it holds the buttons to run, check, clean up, restore and edit each job. Each job backs up its selected folders into its own encrypted repository.

docs.title: Create a job
docs.text:
1. Click + New job (top right). If no job exists yet, the page shows Create the first job instead.
  2. Enter a Job name.
  3. Work through the tabs of the job editor:
    • What to back up and Exclusions
    • Destination
    • Schedule
    • Retention & checks
    • Options
  4. Click Save.

When you save, Keepsake checks the settings. Problems are listed in red next to the Save button and the job is not saved. If the destination holds no repository yet, Keepsake asks you to confirm creating one and then shows the recovery key (see Destination).

A new job starts with these defaults: one schedule, daily at 22:00, incremental; keep one backup per day for 14 days, one per week for 8 weeks and one per month for 12 months; clean up and check every 7 days; VSS on; 2 retries after 15 minutes.

docs.title: Clone a job
docs.text:
Clone on a job card opens the job editor for a new job with all settings of that job: folders and exclusions, destination (location, USB disks, SFTP host, port, user, host key), share logins (user names only), schedules, retention and checks, notifications and options. The name gets (copy) appended; change it to the name you want. The copy must have a name of its own.

Passwords and keys are not copied – not the repository password, not the SFTP password or private key, not the share passwords. Enter them on the Destination tab (and in the share list on the Options tab), then decide where the copy stores its backups:

  • Same location: enter the repository password of the original job. Both jobs then write into the same repository. Each job keeps its own snapshots, cleanup and restore list (they are kept apart by job name), and data both jobs back up is stored only once.
  • New location: change the folder, USB folder or SFTP path. When you save, Keepsake creates a new repository there, asks for a new repository password and shows the new recovery key.

Nothing changes on the original job. A clone is saved only when you click Save.

docs.title: What a job card shows
docs.text:
Element Meaning Coloured dot and state text State of the job (see below). The colour follows the state of the last run. → ... The destination: a path, USB disk <label> \<folder> or sftp://user@host/path. Last run Start time, duration, number of files and the amount of new data of the last run. — if the job never ran. Schedule All schedule entries, for example daily at 22:00 (incremental) · Sat at 23:00 (full). Manual only if the job has no schedule. Next Time of the next automatic run (or a pending retry), followed by how long ago the last successful backup was. Shows Disabled or No schedule when nothing is planned. Message line For runs that did not succeed: the error or warning summary of the last run.

While a run is active, the card shows a progress bar, the number of files, the bytes read and stored, and the file currently being processed.

docs.title: State texts
docs.text:
Text Meaning Last backup OK The last run finished without problems. Last backup with warnings The run finished, but some items were not backed up (for example locked files). Open History for the list. Last backup FAILED The run did not create a backup. The message line shows why. Last backup cancelled Someone cancelled the last run. Never run The job has no run yet. Disabled Scheduled runs are switched off (see below). Waiting for a free slot The run is queued because the maximum number of parallel jobs is already running. Phase name While running: Starting, Pre-command, Creating VSS snapshot, Opening repository, Backing up, Checking, Cleaning up, Post-command and so on.

The state text also covers checks and cleanups: these appear as runs of the job, too.

docs.title: Actions on a card
docs.text:
Button What it does Run now Starts an incremental backup immediately. Full backup Starts a full backup immediately. Cancel Stops the running or queued run of this job after a confirmation. Data already stored is kept and reused by the next run. A queued run is simply removed. Edit Opens the job editor. Not available while the job runs. Clone Opens the job editor for a new job with the same settings, without passwords and keys. See Clone a job. Check Verifies the repository now (integrity check). It reads the share of data set on the Retention & checks tab. Clean up Applies the retention rules now and frees space. Only works if the job has retention rules; otherwise Keepsake reports that there is nothing to clean up. History Opens History and logs filtered to this job. Restore Opens Restoring files for this job. Check keys Opens Check password or recovery key: test the repository password or the recovery key (KS1-...) from your KeePass entry without restoring. Only the repository's key files are read; nothing is changed, stored or logged. See Passwords and keys. Delete Deletes the job and its run history after a confirmation.

Run now, Full backup, Edit, Check, Clean up and Delete are greyed out while the job is running or queued. Run now and Full backup are also greyed out for a disabled job.

docs.title: Full and incremental backups
docs.text:
Every backup is a complete snapshot of the selected files; you can restore any snapshot on its own. The two modes differ only in how files are read:

  • Incremental reads only files whose size or modification time changed since the last backup. Unchanged files are taken over from the previous snapshot. This is fast.
  • Full re-reads every file instead of trusting size and modification time. It is slower but catches changes that did not update the modification time.

In both modes only new data is stored, so a full backup does not double the repository size.

docs.title: Delete a job
docs.text: Deleting removes the job definition and its run history from this server. The backups in the destination are not deleted. You can still restore them with Keepsake Recovery, using the location and the repository password or recovery key from your KeePass entry (see Disaster recovery). A running job cannot be deleted; cancel it first.

docs.title: Disabled jobs
docs.text:
Clear Enabled (scheduled runs active) at the top of the job editor to disable a job. A disabled job:

  • starts no scheduled runs, no catch-up runs and no retries,
  • sends no "no successful backup" alert,
  • cannot be started with Run now or Full backup.

Check, Clean up, Restore and Check keys still work.

docs.title: Parallel jobs
docs.text: Keepsake runs at most as many jobs at the same time as set in Jobs that may run at the same time on the Settings page (1 to 8, default 1). Further runs wait in a queue and show Waiting for a free slot. One job never runs twice at the same time: a scheduled run that becomes due while the same job is still running is skipped (see Schedule). Checks and cleanups that follow a backup wait behind the backup of the same job.

docs.title: Monitoring and notifications
docs.text: Keepsake reports the result of every run in three ways: e-mail notifications, entries in the Windows Event Log and the keepsake status command for scripts. A separate alert fires when a job has had no successful backup for a set number of hours, which also catches jobs that silently stopped running. Use whichever fits your existing monitoring.

docs.title: E-mail notifications
docs.text:
E-mail needs an SMTP server in Settings. Which events send a mail is set per job, in the job editor on the Retention & checks tab under Notifications (e-mail, see Settings) (see Retention and checks):

Switch Default Sends a mail when When a run fails on Any run of the job (backup, restore, check, cleanup) fails. When a run has warnings (files not backed up) on Any run of the job finishes with warnings. After every successful backup off A backup finishes successfully (not checks, cleanups or restores). Alert if no successful backup for … hours (0 = off) 0 See below. Allowed: 0–2160 hours (90 days).

Cancelled runs send no mail.

The subject looks like [Keepsake] FAILED: fileserver – backup on SRV01 (FAILED, WARNING or OK). The body lists job, server, run type and trigger, run ID, start time and duration, the result with its message, the file counts and the first 30 problems from the issue list. It ends with where to find the full log (History & logs, or keepsake log <run-id>).

If a mail cannot be sent, the service writes the reason to its log and to the Event Log (ID 1005). Use Send test e-mail in Settings to check the configuration.

docs.title: "No successful backup" alert
docs.text:
Set Alert if no successful backup for … hours to a value above 0 to be warned when a job has not backed up successfully for that long. A backup with warnings counts as successful. For a new job, the time counts from when the job was created.

  • The alert is checked only for enabled jobs and not while the job is running.
  • It writes Event Log ID 1004 and the service log, and sends the mail [Keepsake] NO BACKUP: <job> on <computer> – since <time> if e-mail is configured.
  • While the condition lasts, it repeats once per alert period (for example every 26 hours with a value of 26).

Tip

Choose a value somewhat above the schedule interval: for a daily backup, 26 or 30 hours leaves room for a slow run without false alarms.

docs.title: Windows Event Log
docs.text:
The service writes important events to the Application log with the source Keepsake:

ID Level Event 1000 Information A run (backup, restore, check, cleanup) succeeded. 1001 Error A run failed. The message contains the reason. 1002 Warning A run finished with warnings. 1003 Warning A scheduled backup was skipped because the previous run was still running, or was missed while the service was not running and catch-up is off for the job. 1004 Error No successful backup for longer than the job's alert period. 1005 Warning An e-mail notification could not be sent.

Events 1000–1002 end with the run ID, the job ID and the start time. Cancelled runs write no event.

The service registers the source at start-up, which needs administrator rights once (the service runs as LocalSystem, so this normally happens automatically). keepsake doctor shows whether the source is registered.

docs.title: Connect your monitoring tool
docs.text:
Any tool that reads the Windows Event Log can alert on Keepsake (PRTG, Zabbix, Nagios/Icinga, SCOM, Checkmk and others). A typical setup:

  • Alert on source Keepsake, IDs 1001 and 1004 (errors).
  • Warn on IDs 1002, 1003 and 1005.
  • Optionally use 1000 as a heartbeat: no 1000 event within the expected time means the backup did not run.

To test a filter, query the log in PowerShell:

Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{ LogName = 'Application'; ProviderName = 'Keepsake' } -MaxEvents 20

docs.title: Status for scripts
docs.text:
keepsake status shows the service and the state, last run, last result and next run of every job. Add --json for machine-readable output: an object with service (version, host, start time, data folder, running runs) and jobs (one entry per job, including the last run and its state). With --json the command exits with code 0 whenever it could query the service; evaluate the job states in the JSON.

Commands that run something (keepsake run <job> --wait, backup, check …) return exit codes your scripts can use: 0 success, 1 warnings, 2 failed, 3 usage error, 4 wrong password or key, 5 repository locked, 6 cancelled.

Service commands need the application password; in scripts pass it with --app-password-file <file>. See Command line.

docs.title: Recovery mode
docs.text: Recovery mode restores straight from a backup location. It does not need the Keepsake service, an application password or a backup job – only the location of the repository and its repository password or recovery key. Use it on a replacement computer after losing a server, on a computer where Keepsake is not installed (portable ZIP), or when the service is not reachable. Once a backup is open, you work on the same restore page as with the service.

docs.title: Start recovery mode
docs.text:
From How Start menu Keepsake Recovery (installed with the MSI) Keepsake GUI Restore from a backup location… on the first-start page, the login page and the Restore page (when there are no jobs) Service not reachable Restore without the service… on the error screen Command line KeepsakeGui.exe --recovery Portable ZIP Keepsake Recovery.cmd

Recovery mode runs with the rights of the logged-on administrator. The header always shows Keepsake Backup · Recovery so you can tell it apart from normal operation.

docs.title: Open a backup
docs.text:
The Open a backup screen asks for:

Field What to enter Where is the backup? The folder that contains keepsake.json. Use Browse… for a local folder. SFTP password Only for SFTP locations: the password of the storage account. or private key file Only for SFTP: an OpenSSH or PuTTY key file (.ppk, .pem, .key, id_*). If set, the password field is ignored. Key passphrase (if the key has one) Only for SFTP with an encrypted key file. Unlock with Repository password or Recovery key (KS1-…). Password / key box The repository password, or the recovery key text. Load from file… reads the key from a text file. Write a debug log (SFTP connection details for support, no passwords) Writes %TEMP%\keepsake-debug.log; the path is shown below the checkbox.

Location formats:

Storage Example USB disk or local folder E:\Keepsake\Fileserver Network share \\server\backup\fileserver SFTP sftp://user@host/path or sftp://user@host:port/path (for example sftp://u123456@u123456.your-storagebox.de:23/backups/fileserver)

Note

A network share that needs a login is not connected by recovery mode. Connect it in Explorer first (or with net use), then enter the UNC path.

Click Open backup. On success, the restore page opens with the backups found in the repository. Errors appear in red above the button, for example The password is not valid for this repository. or No Keepsake repository found at <location>. See Troubleshooting.

Where to find the location, passwords and the recovery key: Passwords and keys.

docs.title: Confirm the SFTP host key
docs.text:
On the first connection to an SFTP server, Keepsake shows the dialog Unknown host key with the server's fingerprint (SHA256:…). Compare it with the fingerprint you recorded, for example in the job's KeePass entry. Click Yes to trust it for this session; No stops with Host key not trusted – not connected.

If the server presents a different key than expected, the connection is refused with a message that the host key has CHANGED. Verify with the server administrator before you continue.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
After opening, the page works like Restoring files, with these differences:

  • Job lists the job names found in the backups. Backups without a job name appear as (backups without job name).
  • Protect this backup is not available; protection needs the service.
  • The restore runs in the GUI process, not in the service. It does not appear in History and logs; use Show log to see the result and the full log before you close the backup.

docs.title: The lock dialog
docs.text:
Before a restore, Keepsake checks the repository for current exclusive locks. A computer that crashed during a cleanup leaves an exclusive lock that blocks restores. In that case the dialog Backup locked shows whose lock it is (purpose, computer, process, user, since when). The lock expires by itself 30 minutes after that computer stopped working on the backup.

  • Click Yes to remove only the locks that block the restore and start it. Do this when that computer is lost or no longer runs Keepsake.
  • Click No to cancel: Restore not started: the backup is locked. Try again in 30 minutes, or remove the lock.

docs.title: What recovery mode changes in the repository
docs.text:
Opening and browsing only read the repository. A restore writes a temporary lock file into the repository's locks folder and removes it at the end. Removing another computer's lock (see above) also deletes that lock file. Backup data, snapshots and keys are never changed.

Warning

The storage account needs write access, even for a restore. A read-only share or SFTP account cannot be used for restores.

docs.title: Leave recovery mode
docs.text:
• Open another backup closes the current backup and returns to Open a backup. It is disabled while a restore runs.
  • Back to the service closes the backup and connects to the Keepsake service on this computer (login page).

  • Passwords and keys – what you need to keep, and where.

docs.title: Restoring files
docs.text: The Restore page brings back folders and files from a backup of one of your jobs. You pick a job and a point in time, tick what you need in the folder tree, choose where it goes and what happens to files that already exist. The Keepsake service does the work and logs the restore like any other run. To restore without the service, without a login or without a job – for example on a replacement computer – use recovery mode instead.

docs.title: Pick the job and the point in time
docs.text:
1. Open Restore in the sidebar.
  2. Select the job under Job.
  3. Select the point in time under Backup from. The newest backup is selected first.

Each entry in Backup from shows:

Part Example Meaning Local time 2026-11-20 22:00 When the backup started. protected · protected The backup is never removed by the retention rules. Mode · incremental / · full How the backup read the files. Both kinds contain the complete file set. Size · 48,210 files, 112 GB Number of files and total size in this backup.

Note

The list shows every backup in the job's repository. If several jobs or computers write to the same repository, their backups appear here as well. The label does not show the job or computer name.

docs.title: Select folders and files
docs.text:
The tree starts at the level that contains the backed-up folders. The line above it (In D:\Data) shows where you are. Folders are shown in bold with their modification time; files show size and modification time.

  • Tick a folder to restore it with everything below it. Items inside a ticked folder are ticked and greyed out.
  • Tick single files to restore only those.
  • The line below the tree shows how many items are selected, or Nothing selected – tick folders or files on the left.

docs.title: Choose the target
docs.text:
Under Restore to:

  • A different folder (default) – enter a folder or pick one with …. It is created if it does not exist.
    • Without Keep the full original path (D\Data\…), each ticked item lands directly in the target folder. Ticking D:\Data\Finance and restoring to E:\Restore gives E:\Restore\Finance.
    • With Keep the full original path (D\Data\…), the drive and the full path are recreated below the target: E:\Restore\D\Data\Finance.
  • The original location – files go back to where they were backed up from (D:\Data\Finance).

Restores never follow a junction or symbolic link below the target folder (or below the backed-up folder when you restore to the original location).

docs.title: Decide what happens to existing files
docs.text:
If a file already exists offers four policies. A file that is identical to the backed-up version (same size and modification time) is always left alone and counted as "already up to date".

Policy Effect Keep the existing file (default) The existing file stays; the backed-up version is not written. Replace if the backup is newer Replaces the file only if the backed-up version has a newer modification time. Always replace Replaces the existing file. Restore as a copy (name (restored 1).ext) Writes the backed-up version next to the existing file as name (restored 1).ext, name (restored 2).ext, …

Kept files appear in the run's issue list as skipped with the reason.

Warning

The original location together with Always replace overwrites the current versions. Keepsake asks for confirmation before it starts.

docs.title: Dry run
docs.text: Tick Dry run – only show what would happen to run the restore without writing anything. The result line and the log show how many files would be restored, kept or left alone. Use it before a large restore to the original location.

docs.title: Start the restore and follow it
docs.text:
1. Click Start restore. The button is available once a backup is selected, at least one item is ticked and a target folder is set (or The original location is chosen).
  2. A progress bar and a status line appear: Restoring: <files> files, <size> written · <current path>. Waiting… means the service has queued the restore because the maximum number of parallel jobs is reached (see Settings).
  3. When it ends, the result line shows the state and the counts, for example SUCCESS: 1,204 restored, 3 already up to date, 0 kept, 0 failed. A dry run adds (dry run).
  4. Click Show log to open the run detail window: summary, issue list, phases and the full log. See History and logs.

A restore is a run of the job. You cannot start it while the job is running or waiting to run ('<job>' is already running or waiting to run.). The Restore page has no cancel button; Cancel on the Backup jobs page or keepsake cancel <job> stops the job's current run, including a restore.

docs.title: Protect a backup
docs.text: Click Protect this backup next to Backup from to keep the selected backup forever: retention rules never remove a protected backup. The label then shows protected and the button changes to Remove protection. You cannot change protection while the job is running. See Retention and checks.

docs.title: What is restored and what is not
docs.text:
Restored Not restored File contents NTFS permissions (ACLs) and owner Creation and last-write time of files and folders Files that were not backed up (see the backup's issue list) File attributes (read-only, hidden, system, archive …); for folders hidden and system

NTFS permissions are not part of the backup. Restored files and folders inherit the permissions of the target folder.

Warning

Restore confidential data only into folders whose permissions are suitable. A restore of the payroll folder into C:\Temp makes it readable for everyone who can read C:\Temp.

The service runs as LocalSystem and writes the files with its rights. For a network target folder, the computer account needs write access to the share.

docs.title: Restore from another computer's backups
docs.text:
• On a computer without Keepsake jobs, or without the service – use recovery mode. You only need the backup location and its password or recovery key.
  • Through the service – a job whose destination points to the existing repository shows all its backups, including those of other computers. Prefer recovery mode if you do not want this computer to back up into that repository.

If the computer has no jobs yet, the Restore page says so and offers Restore from a backup location…, which starts recovery mode. For the full procedure after losing a server, see Disaster recovery.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The Settings page holds the settings of the Keepsake service on this computer: how many jobs may run at the same time, how long run logs are kept, the debug log, the SMTP server for e-mail notifications and the application password. Everything that belongs to a single backup job – sources, destination, schedule, retention, which events send a mail – is set in the job editor instead (see The Backup jobs page).

At the top, the page shows the Keepsake version, the computer name, since when the service runs and its Data folder (by default %ProgramData%\Keepsake).

Each section has its own Save button. A message next to the button confirms Saved. or explains what is wrong.

docs.title: Service
docs.text:
Field Default Allowed Meaning Jobs that may run at the same time 1 1–8 Maximum number of runs (backup, restore, check, cleanup) the service executes in parallel. Further runs wait as Queued. Keep run logs for (days) 90 1–3650 Run logs older than this are deleted. … and at most (runs per job) 200 1–10000 Only this many newest runs per job are kept. Write a debug log (SFTP connection details for support, no passwords) off Writes SFTP connection details to a log file for support.

Both retention limits apply: a run is deleted when it is too old or beyond the number of runs. The service cleans up once a day. Runs that are still queued or running are never deleted. See History and logs.

When the debug log is on, the page shows its path: %ProgramData%\Keepsake\logs\debug.log (only readable by administrators; at most 5 MB, then the older part moves to debug.log.1). It records the SSH algorithms negotiated and connection failures, never passwords or keys. Switch it off again after the support case.

Tip

Raising the number of parallel jobs only helps when jobs write to different destinations. Several jobs reading from the same disk or writing over the same line usually get slower, not faster.

docs.title: E-mail notifications
docs.text:
Leave SMTP server empty to turn e-mail off. Which events send a mail is set per job on the Retention & checks tab of the job editor; see Retention and checks and Monitoring and notifications.

Field Default Meaning SMTP server – Host name or IP address of the mail server. Port / security 587, starttls Port 1–65535 and the encryption. User (optional) – Login name. Leave empty for a relay that accepts mail without login. Password – Login password. Stored encrypted (DPAPI) on this computer. When a password is stored, the page shows A password is stored; leave empty to keep it. From keepsake@<computer name> Sender address. To (; separated) – One or more recipients, separated by ; (or ,). At least one is needed.

Security options:

Option Typical port Behaviour starttls 587 Connects in plain text and switches to TLS (STARTTLS). ssl 465 TLS from the start (implicit SSL). none 25 No encryption. Only for internal relays.

Keepsake uses TLS 1.2 (and TLS 1.3 on Windows Server 2022 and newer). Windows Server 2008 R2 needs TLS 1.2 enabled first; see Windows Server 2008 R2.

Warning

With none and a user name, the password and the report travel in clear text. The service writes a warning to its log each time. Use starttls or ssl whenever the server supports it.

Click Save before Send test e-mail: the test always uses the saved settings. The test sends [Keepsake] Test message from <computer> to all recipients. On success the page shows Test e-mail sent to …; otherwise it shows the reason, for example E-mail could not be sent via mail.example.com:587: ….

Invalid input is rejected on save, for example 'x@' is not a valid e-mail address. or The SMTP port must be between 1 and 65535.

docs.title: Application password
docs.text:
The application password protects access to Keepsake on this computer – this program and the keepsake command line. It is not a repository password and does not encrypt anything; changing it does not affect any backup.

  1. Enter the Current password.
  2. Enter the New password (at least 8 characters) and Repeat new password.
  3. Click Change password. The page confirms Application password changed.

Messages you may see: The new passwords do not match., The current application password is wrong., The application password must have at least 8 characters. Wrong passwords count toward the login lockout (see Troubleshooting).

For the difference between the application password, repository passwords and recovery keys, see Passwords and keys.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists common problems by the symptom or message you see, with the cause and the fix. Messages are quoted as Keepsake shows them; parts in angle brackets vary. If an entry does not solve the problem, run keepsake doctor and collect the logs listed at the end of this page.

docs.title: "The Keepsake service is not reachable."
docs.text: Cause: The Keepsake Backup Service is stopped, not installed, or still starting. Fix: Open services.msc, start Keepsake Backup Service and set it to Automatic; then click Try again. keepsake doctor (elevated) shows the service state. On a computer without Keepsake installed, click Restore without the service… to use recovery mode.

docs.title:
"Wrong application password." / "Too many wrong passwords. Try again in seconds."

Cause: The application password is wrong. After 5 wrong attempts in a row, every further wrong attempt blocks logins for an increasing time (2 s, 4 s, 8 s … up to 5 minutes). Attempts from the GUI and the command line count together. Fix: Wait the time shown and enter the correct password. A correct login resets the counter. The application password is not the repository password; see Passwords and keys.

"The session expired. Please log in again."

Cause: No activity for 30 minutes. Fix: Log in again.

"The password is not valid for this repository." / "The recovery key is not valid for this repository."

Cause: The password or key belongs to another repository, or the password has a typo. Fix: Check that the location is the right repository (each USB disk and each job has its own). Try the recovery key instead of the password, or the other way round. Check keys on the Backup jobs page and keepsake key verify test a password or key without restoring.

"The recovery key contains a typo (checksum mismatch)."

Cause: The recovery key was mistyped. The key carries a checksum, so Keepsake detects typos before trying it. Fix: Copy the key again from KeePass or the key file, or use Load from file…. Dashes and spaces do not matter. This is not a Keepsake recovery key (it must start with 'KS1-'). means the text is not a recovery key at all.

"No Keepsake repository found at ."

Cause: The path does not point to the repository folder, or the disk or share is not connected. Fix: Enter the folder that contains keepsake.json – not its parent or a subfolder. For USB disks, check the drive letter; for SFTP, check the path after the host name. For a job, the message adds Create it in the job settings first.

"The repository is in use by '' on …"

Cause: Another Keepsake process holds a lock on the repository – a running backup, check or cleanup, or a process that crashed. A crashed process leaves a lock that expires after 30 minutes without refresh. Fix: If the named process is still running, wait for it to finish. If not, wait 30 minutes or remove stale locks with keepsake unlock --repo <location>. --all also removes current locks; use it only when you are sure no other Keepsake process works on the repository. Recovery mode offers to remove a blocking lock itself.

keepsake check reports errors

Cause: Missing or damaged files in the repository (disk errors, interrupted copies, manual changes). Fix: If the check reports missing or unreadable index files, run keepsake repair --repo <location>. It rebuilds the index from the pack files; backups and data are not changed. Run keepsake check --repo <location> --read-data afterwards. See Command line.
Backup warnings in the issue list
docs.text:
The run detail window lists every item that was not backed up (see History and logs).

Reason Cause Fix Access denied. The service account cannot read the file, even with the backup privilege. Check the file's permissions; keepsake doctor shows whether the backup privilege is available. File is locked by another program. Enable VSS for the job to back up open files. The file was open and VSS was off or unavailable. Tick Use VSS snapshots so open and locked files are backed up (recommended) on the job's Options tab (Options). Path is too long. The path exceeds what Windows allows for this file. Shorten the path, or exclude it. File was deleted during the backup. The file vanished between listing and reading. Usually harmless (temporary files). Exclude such files to avoid the warning. File changed while it was being backed up; the stored copy may be inconsistent. The file was written during the backup without VSS. Enable VSS. Source folder or file not found – it was not backed up. A selected source no longer exists. Fix the job's sources (What to back up). Junction or symbolic link – the linked folder is not followed. Links are never followed. Add the link target as its own source if you need it.

docs.title:
"VSS snapshot could not be created (). Files are read directly; open or locked files may be skipped."

Cause: The Volume Shadow Copy service is disabled or failed, or there is not enough space for the shadow copy. Fix: Set the Volume Shadow Copy service to Manual (not Disabled); keepsake doctor checks this. Check the System and Application event logs for VSS errors and free space on the volume. No VSS snapshot for this <type> drive is normal for drives that do not support shadow copies (for example network drives).

"None of the USB disks of this job is connected ()."

Cause: No registered disk of the job is attached, or Windows has not mounted it. Fix: Connect one of the listed disks and check that it appears in Explorer. Keepsake recognises disks by volume ID, not drive letter; a new disk must be added to the job first (Destination).

"Cannot connect to \server\share as '': "

Cause: The stored share credentials are wrong or the account has no access. Without credentials, the service connects as the computer account (LocalSystem). Fix: Enter user (DOMAIN\user) and password for the share on the job's Destination tab, or for source shares under Network shares used as sources → Add share on the Options tab. Give the account (or the computer account) write access to the destination share. In recovery mode, connect the share in Explorer first.

Unknown host key

Cause: First connection to this server; the host key is not trusted yet (The host key of <host> is not trusted yet: SHA256:…). Fix: Click Check destination on the job's Destination tab and compare the fingerprint with the one from your provider (for example Hetzner Robot) or ssh-keygen -lf on the server before you confirm. On the command line, pass --sftp-host-key SHA256:….

"WARNING: the host key of has CHANGED …"

Cause: The server was reinstalled, the port changed (a different SSH server answers), or someone intercepts the connection. Fix: Verify the new fingerprint with the server administrator. Only then trust the new key in the job editor (Check destination).

"SFTP login to as '' failed: …"

Cause: Wrong user, password or key, or the key is not authorised on the server. Fix: Check the credentials in the job's Destination tab. The SFTP private key cannot be read: … (does it need a passphrase?) means the key file needs its passphrase or is not a supported format (OpenSSH or PuTTY).

"MAC error" / "MAC error with every algorithm combination the server supports"

Cause: The SSH algorithms do not work between this computer and the server – seen on Windows Server 2008 R2 against servers that only offer AES-CTR. Fix: Run keepsake sftp-test --repo sftp://user@host:port/path on the affected computer; it shows which algorithms work and writes a detailed log. For a Hetzner Storage Box, use port 23 (OpenSSH, offers AES-GCM) instead of port 22 – the job editor offers Use port 23. Port 23 has its own host key. See Windows Server 2008 R2.

Collecting SFTP details for support

Switch on Write a debug log (SFTP connection details for support, no passwords) in Settings (%ProgramData%\Keepsake\logs\debug.log) or, in recovery mode, on the Open a backup screen (%TEMP%\keepsake-debug.log). Reproduce the problem and send the file together with the keepsake sftp-test output.

Test e-mail or notifications do not arrive

Cause: Wrong server, port or security setting; the server rejects the login or the sender; or TLS 1.2 is not enabled (Windows Server 2008 R2). Fix:

  1. Click Send test e-mail in Settings and read the message (E-mail could not be sent via <host>:<port>: …).
  2. Match port and security: 587 with starttls, 465 with ssl.
  3. On Windows Server 2008 R2, run Enable-Tls12.ps1 from the install folder as administrator and reboot. keepsake doctor shows TLS 1.2 (SChannel) as OK afterwards.
  4. Check the spam folder and whether the server accepts the From address.

Failed notifications are logged in the service log and as Event Log ID 1005 (Monitoring).
Check this computer: keepsake doctor
docs.text: Run keepsake doctor in an elevated prompt. It checks the Windows version, .NET Framework 4.8, elevation, the Keepsake service and its interface, TLS 1.2 and .NET strong crypto, the Volume Shadow Copy service, the Event Log source, the permissions of the data folder, the backup privilege and free space on the system drive. Each line is OK, INFO, WARN or FAIL with a hint. Add --json for machine-readable output.
